name: SAM
aliases: SAcrospinous hysteropexy versus the Manchester procedure
question: Is sacrospinous hysteropexy noninferior to the Manchester procedure for composite 2-year success after a first uterus-preserving operation for uterine descent?

design.blinding: open-label; postoperative POP-Q performed by an examiner other than the operating surgeon
design.population: Adults undergoing a first operation for symptomatic prolapse with uterine descent at POP-Q point D at or proximal to −1 cm, without prior pelvic floor surgery or a need for concomitant anti-incontinence surgery.
design.description: Multicenter, unblinded noninferiority randomized trial in 26 Dutch hospitals
design.locator: JAMA 2023;330:626-635, Abstract and Methods (Study Design; Participants and Recruitment; Randomization and Interventions)

verdictNote: Sacrospinous hysteropexy missed the 9% margin in both analyses; only the anatomic component differed significantly.
takeaway: In a first uterus-preserving operation for uterine descent not beyond the hymen, sacrospinous hysteropexy failed the 9% noninferiority margin against the Manchester procedure: 2-year composite success was 77.0% versus 87.3% (difference −10.3%, 95% CI −17.8 to −2.8).

reports.label: Two-year randomized report
reports.citation: Enklaar RA, Schulten SFM, van Eijndhoven HWF, et al. Manchester procedure vs sacrospinous hysteropexy for treatment of uterine descent: a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA.* 2023;330(7):626-635. doi:10.1001/jama.2023.13140
reports.followUp: 2 years; primary outcome complete in 393 of 430 analyzed participants (196 and 197)

results.measure: 2-year composite success, as-randomized analysis; risk difference in percentage points (sacrospinous hysteropexy minus Manchester procedure)
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin −9 percentage points (Farrington-Manning test); the lower confidence limit of −17.8 fell below it. Noninferiority P = 0.65 in the Results text (the Abstract gives 0.63). Success required no prolapse beyond the hymen in any compartment, no bothersome bulge symptoms and no pessary or surgical retreatment.
results.locator: JAMA Table 2 and Primary Outcome text; Abstract

results.measure: 2-year composite success, per-protocol analysis; risk difference in percentage points (sacrospinous hysteropexy minus Manchester procedure)
results.note: Noninferiority had to be shown in both the as-randomized and per-protocol populations; noninferiority P = 0.62.
results.locator: JAMA Table 2 and Primary Outcome text

harms.label: Participants with a serious adverse event
harms.note: Table 3 prints 4.7% and 5.1%, which do not reconcile with its column totals of 207 and 213 participants.

harms.label: Death
harms.locator: JAMA Table 3 and Adverse Events text
harms.note: One Manchester participant died 5 weeks after surgery of a suspected massive pulmonary embolism, plausibly related to surgery; the other five deaths were judged unlikely to be study related (malignancy 2, Alzheimer disease 1, cardiovascular incident 1, COVID-19 1).

harms.label: Urinary retention following treatment
harms.note: Repetitive residual urine above 150 mL or catheterization beyond 24 hours after first Foley removal.

harms.label: Blood loss above 500 mL
harms.note: No blood transfusions or injuries to adjacent organs in either group.

harms.label: Reoperation for a reason other than prolapse
harms.note: In the sacrospinous hysteropexy group this included 3 suture removals (1.4%).

harms.label: Rehospitalization for a reason other than prolapse
Buttock pain requiring extra visits or treatment
harms.locator: JAMA Table 3 and Adverse Events text
harms.note: Table 3 prints 2.3% for 5/207, which computes to 2.4%. With treatment 4/207 (1.9%): severe in 1 and persistent for at least 2 months in 3. Three had suture removal (at 2 days, 4 months and 6 months) and another prolapse operation (Manchester procedure 2, vaginal hysterectomy 1); 3 had a local nerve block.

harms.label: Cervical stenosis
harms.note: Presented with postmenopausal bleeding in one and dysmenorrhea with hematometra in the other.

delivery.label: Surgeons and technique standardization
delivery.value: 72 gynecologic surgeons in 26 hospitals, each with at least 20 of both procedures (at least 10 of each in the preceding 2 years); techniques agreed before enrollment

delivery.label: Sacrospinous hysteropexy technique
delivery.value: Unilateral fixation of the posterior cervix to the right sacrospinous ligament with 2 nonabsorbable sutures

delivery.label: Manchester procedure technique
delivery.value: Extraperitoneal plication of the uterosacral ligaments at the posterior side of the uterus, cervical amputation and plication of the cardinal ligaments on the anterior side of the cervix

delivery.label: Randomized and analyzed

values.exp: 217 randomized; 215 after 2 exclusions (196 analyzed for the primary outcome)
values.ctl: 217 randomized; 215 after 2 exclusions (197 analyzed for the primary outcome)

delivery.locator: JAMA Results, Protocol Violations and Adverse Events; Table 2
delivery.note: Exclusions (0.9% per group) were for a predefined exclusion criterion met at randomization.

delivery.label: Major protocol violations
delivery.value: 12 participants: 2 randomized to the Manchester procedure received hysteropexy and 5 randomized to hysteropexy received a Manchester procedure; 4 received a nonstudy procedure instead of hysteropexy (1 vaginal hysterectomy, 3 colporrhaphy without apical reconstruction); 1 had concomitant sphincter ani repair
delivery.locator: JAMA Results, Protocol Violations and Adverse Events
delivery.note: Included in the as-randomized analysis and excluded from the per-protocol analysis.

delivery.label: Histology of amputated cervices
delivery.value: 164 (80.4%) specimens examined; 4 abnormal, including 1 CIN2 in a patient with no preoperative Papanicolaou test

reports.label: Economic evaluation
reports.citation: Schulten SFM, Enklaar RA, Weemhoff M, et al. Economic evaluation of Manchester procedure versus sacrospinous hysteropexy: a follow-up analysis of a randomized clinical trial. *PLoS One.* 2025;20(11):e0336030. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0336030
reports.followUp: 2 years; complete data for 84% of QALYs (n = 363), 72% of healthcare costs and 58% of societal costs

results.measure: Mean 2-year societal cost in euros at 2019 prices (multiple imputation, base case); mean difference, Manchester procedure minus sacrospinous hysteropexy
results.note: Complete-case analysis: €9,526.79 with sacrospinous hysteropexy versus €7,996.13 with the Manchester procedure (Manchester minus hysteropexy −€1,530.65, 95% CI −2,952.53 to −108.77). The difference arose mainly from indirect (productivity) costs.

results.measure: Mean 2-year direct healthcare cost in euros at 2019 prices (multiple imputation); mean difference, Manchester procedure minus sacrospinous hysteropexy

delivery.note: The cost table lists the Capio device (Boston Scientific).

reports.label: Sexual function at 24 months
reports.citation: Stoter LM, Peters K, Enklaar RA, et al. Sexual function after the Manchester procedure versus sacrospinous hysteropexy in women treated for uterine prolapse: a planned analysis of a randomized clinical trial. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2026;234(4):1112-1120. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2025.12.035
reports.followUp: 24 months; 393 women completed the questionnaire at baseline and 24 months

results.measure: Mean change in PISQ-IR score from baseline to 24 months in sexually active participants (Manchester procedure n = 101, sacrospinous hysteropexy n = 99); mean difference, Manchester procedure minus sacrospinous hysteropexy
results.note: Equivalence design with a predefined margin of ±0.31 points, the minimally clinically important difference; the abstract states that the interval lies entirely within the margin.

results.endpoint: De novo dyspareunia, sexually active participants
results.measure: De novo dyspareunia at 24 months among participants sexually active at baseline
results.note: Abstract reports a 95% CI of 0.1% to 16.5% and no significant difference between groups.

results.endpoint: De novo dyspareunia including women who became sexually inactive
results.measure: De novo dyspareunia at 24 months after counting outcomes of women who became nonsexually active after surgery
results.note: Abstract reports a 95% CI of 1.5% to 13.9%.

results.endpoint: Condition-impact score in sexually inactive participants
results.measure: Change in PISQ-IR condition-impact score in participants not sexually active (Manchester procedure n = 59, sacrospinous hysteropexy n = 64)
results.note: No differences between procedures; 24% of those inactive before surgery (Manchester procedure n = 20, sacrospinous hysteropexy n = 19) were sexually active at 24 months.

relations.note: SAM took SAVE-U's lower 5-year anatomic recurrence after hysteropexy as rationale; it compared hysteropexy with the Manchester procedure instead of hysterectomy.
